DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-01: Purpose and Scope

This policy explains annual leave entitlement, accrual,
approval, and recordkeeping at DemoCo.

It applies to full-time employees working the standard
Monday-to-Friday schedule.

Part-time employees, interns, and contractors are outside
the scope of this policy. Their arrangements must be
confirmed with Human Resources.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-02: Entitlement and Accrual

Eligible employees receive 25 working days of annual leave
for a complete calendar year of service.

The leave year runs from January 1 to December 31.

Leave accrues from the employee's joining date at a rate
of 25/12 days per complete calendar month of service.
A partial calendar month does not earn leave under this
fictional policy.

Accrual calculations retain their full precision.
Balances are displayed to two decimal places.

Leave may be requested in half-day or full-day increments.
Displayed rounding does not create additional entitlement.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-03: Submitting a Request

Employees must submit requests through the HR system at
least 10 calendar days before the proposed start date.

Each request must include:
- The requested start and end dates.
- The number of working days requested.
- A brief handover plan.
- The name of the proposed colleague covering urgent work,
  where applicable.

Employees should avoid making non-refundable travel
arrangements before receiving approval.

Urgent requests with shorter notice may be considered by
the line manager and HR, but approval is not guaranteed.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-04: Approval and Operational Coverage

All annual leave requires line-manager approval.

Managers consider available leave balance, staffing levels,
overlapping requests, operational commitments, and handover
arrangements.

Having sufficient leave balance does not guarantee approval.

Managers should respond within five working days.
A request remains pending until explicitly approved;
a delayed response does not count as approval.

Employees must not begin leave while a request is pending
or rejected.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-05: Balance Calculation and Deductions

The available balance is calculated as:

Available balance =
accrued current-year entitlement
+ valid unused carryover
- current-year leave already taken
- approved future leave

Approved future leave is reserved immediately so that the
same balance cannot be used for another request.

When approved leave is taken, it moves from the reserved
amount to the taken amount and is not deducted twice.

Pending and rejected requests do not reduce the balance.

Standard requests cannot exceed the available balance.
Requests to use unaccrued leave require separate written
approval from HR and the line manager and are outside the
standard calculation process.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-06: Counting Leave Days

Annual leave is counted in working days.

For the standard Monday-to-Friday schedule, Saturdays and
Sundays are excluded.

Dates listed in DemoCo's approved public-holiday calendar
are also excluded.

For example, leave from Monday through the following
Sunday counts as five working days when no public holiday
falls within that period.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-07: Carryover and Expiry

Employees may carry over up to five unused accrued days
into the next calendar year.

Carryover is recorded by HR after the year-end balance
review. Days already taken or committed to approved future
leave cannot also be carried over.

Carried-over days must be used by March 31 of the new year.
They are used before current-year entitlement.

Any unused carryover expires after March 31 unless the
Head of HR approves a written exception before that date.

Unused days above the five-day limit expire at year-end
unless a written exception has been approved.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-08: Changes and Cancellations

Employees must request changes or cancellations through
the HR system.

Changes to approved dates require fresh manager approval.

When a cancellation is approved, the associated reserved
days are released back to the available balance.

If leave is shortened after it has started, HR must verify
the actual return-to-work date before restoring unused days.

Expired carryover is not automatically restored through
a cancellation. HR must review such cases.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-09: Handover and Return to Work

Before leave begins, employees must update outstanding
tasks, share necessary handover information, and activate
an out-of-office message identifying an appropriate contact.

Employees must return on their next scheduled working day
after the approved leave ends.

If an unexpected event prevents their return, they must
notify the line manager and HR as soon as reasonably possible.
An extension requires approval.

DemoCo Annual Leave Policy
AL-10: Records, Disputes, and Exceptions

HR maintains the official leave records.

Employees who identify an incorrect balance should contact
HR with the relevant request details. The disputed balance
must be verified before additional leave is confirmed.

Exceptions must be documented with the approver's name,
approval date, and reason.

This policy does not define sick leave, unpaid leave,
leave encashment, or final-settlement calculations.
Questions on these topics must be referred to the
relevant policy or HR.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-01: Purpose and Scope

This policy describes DemoCo's learning allowance,
wellbeing reimbursement, and company equipment arrangements.

It applies to full-time employees.

Part-time employees, interns, and contractors must confirm
their benefits with HR. Eligibility must not be assumed.

Benefits are subject to the conditions in each section.
An available allowance does not guarantee approval.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-02: Learning and Development Allowance

Full-time employees who have successfully completed
probation may claim up to AED 2,000 per calendar year
for approved professional development.

Eligible expenses include job-related courses,
certification examinations, and professional workshops.

The allowance becomes available on the effective date
of probation confirmation recorded by HR.

The annual limit is not prorated in the confirmation year.

Unused allowance does not carry over and cannot be
exchanged for cash.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-03: Learning Approval Process

Employees must obtain written approval from their
line manager and HR before enrolling or making payment.

Requests must include:
- The course or examination title.
- The provider.
- The business relevance.
- The total cost.
- The expected completion date.

Approval must specify the maximum reimbursable amount.

Expenses paid before approval are not eligible under
the standard process. Exceptions require written
approval from the Head of HR.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-04: Learning Reimbursement

Employees must submit a claim within 30 calendar days
after completing the approved activity.

The claim must include the approval, an itemized receipt,
proof of payment, and evidence of attendance or completion.

Reimbursement is limited to the lowest of:
- The eligible amount actually paid.
- The approved maximum amount.
- The remaining annual learning allowance.

The expense is allocated to the calendar year in which
the activity is completed.

Pending approved claims reserve the corresponding
allowance. Paid claims must not be deducted twice.

Refunds received from the provider must be reported
to HR so the claim and allowance can be corrected.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-05: Wellbeing Allowance

Full-time employees who have successfully completed
probation may claim up to AED 600 per calendar year
for eligible wellbeing expenses.

Eligible expenses are gym memberships and organized
fitness classes purchased after probation confirmation.

Equipment, clothing, food, supplements, and medical
treatment are not covered by this allowance.

The annual limit is not prorated in the confirmation year.

Unused allowance does not carry over and has no cash value.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-06: Wellbeing Claims

Claims require an itemized receipt and proof of payment.

Employees must submit claims within 30 calendar days
of payment. HR verifies eligibility before reimbursement.

The expense is allocated to the calendar year of payment,
including when a membership extends into the next year.

Reimbursement cannot exceed the eligible amount paid
or the remaining annual wellbeing allowance.

Learning and wellbeing allowances are separate.
Unused funds cannot be transferred between them.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-07: Company Equipment

Company equipment is assigned according to role
requirements and manager approval, including during
probation where needed.

Equipment remains company property and must be recorded
in the asset register.

Employees must report loss, theft, or damage to IT
and their line manager as soon as possible.

Equipment must be returned when requested or when
employment ends.

This policy does not define employee liability or
salary deductions for lost or damaged equipment.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-08: Processing and Payment

HR reviews complete reimbursement claims within
10 working days of submission.

Requests for missing information pause this review period.

Approved claims are scheduled for the next available
payroll cycle, subject to the payroll cutoff.

Submitting a claim does not mean it has been approved.

Employees may contact HR to check the status of a claim.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-09: Exclusions and Missing Information

This policy does not define:
- Medical insurance coverage.
- Housing or transport allowances.
- Flight tickets or travel benefits.
- Relocation assistance.
- Bonuses.
- End-of-service payments.

The HR Copilot must not infer entitlement to these
benefits from this document.

Questions about excluded benefits must be referred
to HR or the relevant policy.

DemoCo Employee Benefits Policy
BN-10: Records and Exceptions

HR maintains the official benefit eligibility and
allowance records.

Claims must not be reimbursed more than once.
An expense cannot be claimed under both allowances.

Exceptions require written approval from the Head of HR,
including the reason, amount, and applicable dates.

An exception for one employee does not automatically
change the rules for other employees.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-01: Purpose and Scope

This policy defines the onboarding, performance review,
and confirmation process for newly hired full-time employees.

It does not apply to interns, contractors, or part-time
employees. Their arrangements must be confirmed with HR.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-02: Standard Probation Period

The standard probation period is three calendar months
from the employee's joining date.

The scheduled review date is calculated by adding three
calendar months to the joining date. If the target month
does not contain the same day number, its last day is used.

For example, an employee joining on January 15 has a
scheduled review date of April 15.

Reaching the scheduled review date does not automatically
confirm employment or activate confirmation-dependent benefits.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-03: Onboarding and Objectives

During the first five working days, the line manager
must explain the employee's responsibilities, performance
objectives, and required training.

Objectives must be documented and shared with the employee.

Employees must complete assigned onboarding activities
and raise any access, equipment, or training issues
with their manager.

Role-required equipment may be provided during probation,
as described in the Employee Benefits Policy.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-04: Progress Reviews

The line manager should conduct a progress discussion
approximately one month after joining.

A final probation review should take place before
the scheduled review date.

Reviews consider:
- Progress against agreed objectives.
- Quality and reliability of work.
- Collaboration and communication.
- Completion of required training.
- Attendance records, considered with approved leave.

Managers must document feedback and give employees
an opportunity to respond.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-05: Confirmation Decision

The line manager submits a recommendation to HR.

HR verifies the review and issues the written outcome.

An employee is confirmed only when HR records an approved
confirmation with an explicit effective date.

A manager's verbal statement alone is not confirmation.

The HR record must include the decision, effective date,
approver, and supporting review reference.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-06: Pending or Delayed Reviews

If the review is delayed, the employee or manager should
contact HR.

A pending review must not be treated as either successful
confirmation or unsuccessful completion.

The HR Copilot must use the recorded status and must not
infer confirmation from elapsed service alone.

This policy does not establish an automatic probation
extension. Any proposed change requires HR review and
separate written documentation.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-07: Annual Leave During Probation

Annual leave accrues from the joining date according
to the Annual Leave Policy.

Employees on probation may request accrued annual leave
through the standard approval process.

Requests remain subject to available balance,
notice requirements, and manager approval.

Probation status alone does not create additional
annual leave entitlement.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-08: Sick Leave During Probation

Full-time employees on probation are covered by the
Sick Leave Policy.

The annual sick leave allowance, notification rules,
and medical certificate requirements apply.

Probation status does not remove the requirement
to report absence or provide supporting documents.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-09: Benefits After Confirmation

Learning and wellbeing allowances become available
from the effective confirmation date recorded by HR,
subject to the Employee Benefits Policy.

A scheduled review date or pending recommendation
does not activate these allowances.

Confirmation does not automatically guarantee a
salary increase, bonus, or promotion.

Any compensation change requires separate written approval.

DemoCo Probation and Confirmation Policy
PR-10: Other Outcomes and Questions

If successful confirmation is not recommended,
HR must communicate the outcome and applicable next steps
through the appropriate process.

This policy does not define termination procedures,
notice periods, final settlements, or appeal deadlines.

The HR Copilot must not invent these rules.
Questions about them must be referred to HR or
an applicable approved document.

Employees who believe their status is incorrect should
ask HR to verify the official record.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-01: Purpose and Scope

This policy explains how eligible employees report sickness,
provide supporting documents, and record sick leave.

It applies to full-time employees working the standard
Monday-to-Friday schedule, including employees on probation.

Part-time employees, interns, and contractors must confirm
their arrangements with HR.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-02: Annual Entitlement

Eligible employees receive up to 10 paid working days of
sick leave per calendar year.

The full allowance is available from the joining date.
It is not prorated or accrued monthly.

Unused sick leave does not carry over into the following year
and cannot be exchanged for cash or annual leave.

Absence beyond the allowance requires HR review.
Additional paid or unpaid leave is not automatically granted.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-03: Reporting an Absence

Employees must notify their line manager before their
scheduled starting time on the first day of absence.

If an emergency prevents timely notification, the employee
or a representative must contact the manager as soon as
reasonably possible.

The notification should include the expected duration of
absence, if known. Employees are not required to share
their diagnosis with their manager.

Employees must update the manager if the expected return
date changes.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-04: Recording the Request

Employees must submit a sick leave request through the
HR system within two working days of returning to work.

The request must include the absence dates and any required
supporting documentation.

If the employee cannot access the system, HR may record
the request on their behalf.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-05: Supporting Documents

Absences lasting one or two consecutive scheduled working
days may be self-certified through the HR system.

Absences lasting three or more consecutive scheduled working
days require a medical certificate covering the absence.

Weekends and company-recognized public holidays do not count
toward this threshold and do not break an otherwise
consecutive absence.

For example, absence on Friday, Monday, and Tuesday requires
a medical certificate when all three are scheduled working
days and none is a company-recognized public holiday.

Missing documentation must be referred to HR for review.
The absence is not automatically converted to annual leave.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-06: Counting Sick Leave Days

Sick leave is counted in scheduled working days.

For the standard Monday-to-Friday schedule, Saturdays,
Sundays, and company-recognized public holidays are excluded.

Sick leave may be recorded in half-day or full-day increments.

An absence spanning two calendar years is allocated to
each year according to the working days falling within it.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-07: Verification and Balance

The line manager acknowledges the absence notification.
HR verifies eligibility, documentation, and the remaining
sick leave allowance.

The remaining allowance is calculated as:

Remaining sick leave =
10 days - verified paid sick leave taken in that calendar year

Pending requests must be shown separately and are not
treated as verified paid leave until HR completes its review.

Requests exceeding the remaining allowance must be
referred to HR. The standard tool must not report a
negative paid sick leave balance.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-08: Illness During Annual Leave

Employees who become ill during approved annual leave may
request that eligible days be reclassified as sick leave.

Reclassification requires:
- A medical certificate covering the requested dates.
- Sufficient remaining sick leave allowance.
- HR verification and approval.

A medical certificate is required for reclassification
regardless of the number of days requested.

Only scheduled working days may be reclassified.
Approved reclassification restores the corresponding
annual leave days without counting the same absence twice.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-09: Medical Information and Confidentiality

Medical certificates must be submitted through the
designated HR channel.

Access to medical documents is restricted to authorized
HR personnel.

Managers receive only information needed for attendance,
work arrangements, and operational coverage.

This policy does not authorize storing diagnoses or medical
certificates in the HR Copilot's employee analytics dataset.

DemoCo Sick Leave Policy
SL-10: Return to Work and Exceptions

Employees should confirm their return date with the
line manager.

Any recommended workplace adjustments must be coordinated
with HR through the designated process.

Disputed records and exceptional circumstances require
HR review. The employee must not assume an exception
has been approved.

This policy does not define maternity leave, workplace
injury benefits, or medical insurance coverage.
Questions on those topics must be referred to HR or
the relevant policy.

DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-01: Purpose and Scope

This policy defines the standard working schedule,
attendance expectations, and approval procedures for
changes to working arrangements.

It applies to full-time employees on the standard office
schedule.

Shift workers, part-time employees, interns, and contractors
must confirm their schedules with HR. The standard schedule
must not be assumed to apply to them.

DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-02: Standard Working Schedule

The standard working week is Monday through Friday.

Office hours are 09:00 to 18:00, with a one-hour unpaid
break from 13:00 to 14:00.

This represents eight working hours per day and
40 working hours per week.

Saturdays and Sundays are non-working days for employees
on this schedule.

All times refer to the employee's assigned office location.

metadata.document_title: DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-03: Breaks and Availability

Employees must take their scheduled break and coordinate
coverage where their role requires continuous service.

Changes to the break time require line-manager approval
and do not change the total daily working hours.

During working hours, employees must remain reasonably
available through the company's agreed communication channels.

A full working day is eight working hours.
A half working day is four working hours, excluding breaks.

metadata.document_title: DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-04: Attendance Records

Employees must record their actual start and finish times
in the attendance system.

Employees must not record attendance on behalf of another
person.

If a record is missing or incorrect, the employee must
submit a correction request within two working days of
discovering the issue.

Attendance corrections require line-manager verification.

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-05: Late Arrival and Unexpected Absence

Employees who expect to arrive late must notify their
line manager as soon as possible and provide an estimated
arrival time.

Reporting a delay does not automatically authorize a
schedule change.

Unexpected absence must be reported before the scheduled
starting time where reasonably possible.

Sickness-related absence is handled under the Sick Leave
Policy, including its notification and documentation rules.

metadata.document_title: DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-06: Flexible Working Hours

Employees may request a regular start time between
08:00 and 10:00.

An approved flexible schedule must retain eight working
hours and a one-hour unpaid break per day.

For example, an approved 08:00 start normally corresponds
to a 17:00 finish with a one-hour unpaid break.

Approval must be recorded by the line manager and HR.
Employees must follow the standard schedule until approval
is confirmed.

Flexible hours do not change annual or sick leave entitlement.

metadata.document_title: DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-07: Remote Working

Remote working is not an automatic entitlement.

Employees must obtain written line-manager approval for
the requested dates before working remotely.

Approved remote-working days count as working days,
not leave days.

Employees must follow their approved hours, remain
available, and use company-approved systems.

Requests to work from another country require separate
HR and IT review and are not authorized by ordinary
remote-working approval.

metadata.document_title: DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-08: Additional Hours

Employees must obtain written line-manager approval
before performing additional hours beyond their
approved schedule.

Attendance records alone do not establish entitlement
to additional pay or time off.

This policy does not specify overtime payment rates
or compensatory leave calculations. Such questions
must be referred to HR and Payroll.

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-09: Public Holidays and Temporary Schedules

HR maintains the approved public-holiday calendar.

Company-recognized public holidays are excluded from
annual and sick leave deductions for employees on
the standard schedule.

Temporary changes to office hours must be communicated
through a formal HR notice stating the applicable
dates and employee groups.

The HR Copilot must not invent holiday dates or
temporary schedules when no approved record is available.

text:
DemoCo Working Hours and Attendance Policy
WH-10: Exceptions and Related Policies

Permanent schedule changes require written approval
from HR and the line manager.

Any exception must identify the employee or group,
the approved arrangement, and its effective dates.

Annual leave requests follow the Annual Leave Policy.
Sickness-related absence follows the Sick Leave Policy.

This policy does not define disciplinary penalties,
salary deductions, or special working-hour entitlements.
Questions on these matters must be referred to HR.
